from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Average vs. Instantaneous Speed", [
            "Average speed is total distance over total time.",
            "But what is speed at one specific moment?",
            "Calculus helps us find this instantaneous speed."
        ])
        
        # Setup graph elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[0, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.7)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F4')
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**3, color=WHITE)
        
        # Secant line variables
        point_a = axes.c2p(1, 0.2)
        point_b = axes.c2p(4, 3.2)
        
        secant_line = Line(point_a, point_b, color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Create(secant_line))
        avg_speed_label = Text("Average Speed", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(avg_speed_label, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(avg_speed_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        point_b_tracker = ValueTracker(4)
        def update_secant(mob):
            x = point_b_tracker.get_value()
            new_b = axes.c2p(x, 0.2 * x**3)
            mob.put_start_and_end_on(point_a, new_b)
            mob.set_color("#FF5733")
            
        secant_line.add_updater(update_secant)
        self.play(point_b_tracker.animate.set_value(1.1), run_time=3)
        secant_line.remove_updater(update_secant)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        
        tangent_line = Line(axes.c2p(1, 0.2), axes.c2p(2, 0.4), color="#33FF57")
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.play(Flash(tangent_line, color="#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Limit: From Secant to Tangent", [
            "We plot position versus time on a graph.",
            "A secant line connects two distinct points.",
            "Shrinking the interval makes the secant move.",
            "As interval nears zero, it becomes tangent.",
            "This limit gives us the instantaneous rate."
        ])
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6, 1], y_range=[0, 6, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**3, color=WHITE)
        
        t1 = ValueTracker(1)
        t2 = ValueTracker(3)
        
        def get_secant():
            p1 = axes.c2p(t1.get_value(), 0.2 * t1.get_value()**3)
            p2 = axes.c2p(t2.get_value(), 0.2 * t2.get_value()**3)
            return Line(p1, p2, color="#FF5733")
            
        secant = always_redraw(get_secant)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733").set_opacity(1)
        self.add(secant)
        self.play(Indicate(secant))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57").set_opacity(1)
        self.play(t2.animate.set_value(1.1), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#33FF57").set_opacity(1)
        # Tangent at t=1: f'(x) = 0.6x^2, f'(1) = 0.6
        # Point (1, 0.2), Slope 0.6 => y - 0.2 = 0.6(x - 1) => y = 0.6x - 0.4
        tangent = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.6 * x - 0.4, color="#33FF57")
        self.play(FadeIn(tangent), FadeOut(secant))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW).set_opacity(1)
        self.play(tangent.animate.set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The derivative is the slope of the tangent.",
            "Formula: limit as h approaches zero of slope.",
            "This measures change at an exact point.",
            "Secant slope represents average change over h.",
            "The limit reveals the instantaneous rate."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Derivative", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare formula
        formula = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}")
        formula.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_opacity(1))
        # Highlight f(x+h) - f(x)
        # B029: Use get_part_by_tex
        num = formula.get_part_by_tex(r"f(x+h) - f(x)")
        self.play(num.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_opacity(1))
        # Highlight h
        h_part = formula.get_part_by_tex("h")
        self.play(h_part.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_opacity(1)
        # Animation: h shrinking
        self.play(FadeOut(num), FadeOut(h_part))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_opacity(1)
        final_symbol = MathTex(r"f'(x)")
        self.place_at_grid(final_symbol, "C3", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.play(Flash(final_symbol))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Falling Drone", [
            "Imagine a drone dropping a package.",
            "Height changes according to gravity over time.",
            "The derivative function tells us exact velocity."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        drone = Dot(color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(drone, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(drone))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Position function: s(t) = -4.9t^2
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 2], y_range=[-20, 0], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        graph = axes.plot(lambda t: -4.9 * t**2, color="#00FF00")
        
        # Use VGroup to group axes and graph for easier placement
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, graph)
        self.place_in_area(graph_group, 'C4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(Create(graph_group))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        velocity_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=DOWN*1, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(velocity_arrow, 'C3')
        
        # Updater for drone falling and velocity arrow
        t = ValueTracker(0)
        drone.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(self.grid['B3'] + np.array([0, -4.9 * t.get_value()**2 / 10, 0])))
        velocity_arrow.add_updater(lambda a: a.next_to(drone, DOWN, buff=0.1))
        
        self.play(t.animate.set_value(2), run_time=3)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        
        self.wait(1)

            "Slopes reveal peaks, valleys, and trends."

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem: Average vs. Instantaneous Speed
sections.content: Begin by reviewing 'Average Speed' (Total distance / Total time). Use a visual of a Cheetah running. Contrast this with the 'Speedometer' reading at a single, frozen moment in time. Establish the goal: How do we calculate speed at an exact instant?
sections.example: A Cheetah sprints. We know its average speed over 10 seconds, but how fast is it going at exactly 3.5 seconds?

sections.title: Visualizing the Limit: From Secant to Tangent
sections.content: Introduce a position-time graph. Show a secant line connecting two points (t1, t2). As we shrink the gap between the points (Δt approaching 0), animate the secant line rotating until it becomes a tangent line. This visual transition represents the 'Limit'.
sections.example: Two points on a curve move closer together until they merge into one, showing the slope at a single point.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formalize the concept. Introduce the limit definition of the derivative: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Break down each component: the slope of the secant (rise/run) transforming into the slope of the tangent via the limit.
sections.example: Representing the change in position (f(x+h) - f(x)) divided by the tiny change in time (h).

sections.title: Application: The Falling Drone
sections.content: Apply the derivative to a practical scenario. Use a drone dropping a package. Show how the derivative function (velocity) provides the exact speed at any height, illustrating that the derivative is the 'rate of change' function.
sections.example: A delivery drone drops a package; the derivative of its height equation gives us the exact velocity at any point during the fall.

sections.title: Summary and Intuition Check
sections.content: Summarize that the 'Derivative' is simply the slope of the tangent line, which represents the 'Instantaneous Rate of Change'. Conclude with a quick visual quiz: matching derivative values (slopes) to different points on a mountain profile.
sections.example: Looking at a mountain path: steep positive slope (climbing), zero slope (peak), negative slope (descending).
